verses.1: While that supremely wonderful sacrifice was thus going on, Valmiki, the foremost among sages, quickly arrived with his disciples.
verses.2: Having seen the divine-like and wondrous sacrifice, he (Valmiki) constructed auspicious huts in a secluded spot among the hermitages of other sages.
verses.3: He also had many carts, full of excellent fruits and roots, placed not far off in his charming hermitage.
verses.4: Valmiki, of great splendor and self-controlled, was greatly honored by the king and the great-souled sages, and thus he resided there.
verses.5: Valmiki, delighted, instructed his two disciples to go and sing the entire epic poem of Ramayana with utmost concentration and joy.
verses.6: They were to sing in sacred hermitages of sages, in the homes of Brahmins, in streets, on royal highways, and in the palaces of kings.
verses.7: They should sing especially at Rama's palace gate, where rituals are performed, and in front of the priests.
verses.8: While singing, they should repeatedly taste these various delicious fruits that grow on the mountain peaks.
verses.9: O dear children, you two will not experience fatigue by eating fruits and pure roots, and you will stay outside the city.
verses.10: If King Rama calls for the sages to listen, then the singing should begin.
verses.11: Twenty cantos should be sung daily with a sweet voice, using the many meters and measures as I have previously instructed.
verses.12: Do not show even a little greed for wealth, for what use is wealth to those who live in hermitages and subsist on fruits and roots?
verses.13: If Rama, the descendant of Kakutstha, asks, "Whose boys are you two?", then tell the king, "We are the disciples of Valmiki."
verses.14: Harmonize these very sweet strings or notes in an unprecedented manner, and sing very sweetly, free from any anxiety.
verses.15: The Ramayana should be sung from the beginning, and the king should not be disrespected, for a king is indeed the father of all beings by virtue of dharma.
verses.16: Therefore, you two, with joyful minds, should take your seats tomorrow morning and sing the sweet song, accompanied by string instruments and rhythm.
verses.17: Thus, having repeatedly instructed them, the highly renowned and most noble sage Valmiki, son of Prachetas, then remained silent.
verses.18: Having been instructed by that sage, both sons of Maithili, those subduers of enemies, departed, saying, "We shall do just so."
verses.19: Then, those two princes, having fixed those wonderful words spoken by the sage in their hearts, passed the night with great eagerness, just as the Ashvins awaited the wisdom of Bhargava. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रिनवतितमः सर्गः ।। 93 ।। Thus ends the ninety-third sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
